title: Involving volunteers (guidance hub)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (guidance updated February 2024). The topics NCVO covers: role descriptions, expenses, safeguarding, volunteer policy, insurance, volunteer management systems, recruiting, agreements, induction, keeping and thanking volunteers, volunteers and the law, and the free Investing in Volunteers (IiV) Essentials self-check

title: Writing volunteer role descriptions
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed 12 April 2021). What a role description includes (title, aims, tasks, limits, policies, contact, expenses, how success is measured); it must not read like a job description or imply a contract

title: Writing a volunteer agreement
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed 12 April 2021). Agreements are optional; write hopes and expectations, not obligations; avoid set hours, contract wording and perks; repay expenses after they are incurred; may state it is not a legal contract

title: Paying volunteer expenses
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed 29 March 2023). Reimburse real out-of-pocket costs with receipts; no flat rates, stipends, vouchers or rewards; payments above expenses can create employment rights, count as taxable income and affect benefits; suggests paying within a month

title: Running a volunteer induction
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed 12 April 2021). What an induction covers: the role, people, a tour, who to ask, breaks, expense claims, shadowing, key policies (safeguarding, data protection), complaints, and regular check-ins afterwards

title: Thanking volunteers
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed 12 April 2021). Thank in person or in writing, public or private to suit the person, show impact, thank teams to avoid winners and losers; Volunteers' Week 1 to 7 June and International Volunteer Day 5 December; avoid money, vouchers, valuable or regular gifts

title: Solving volunteer problems
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed 12 April 2021). Keep a volunteer problem-solving process separate from staff discipline; gather facts, hear everyone, agree a solution and review date; end the volunteering only after other solutions fail or for serious problems

title: Safeguarding, vulnerable clients and DBS
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last reviewed 19 May 2022). Risk assess each role for DBS eligibility; a safeguarding policy covers safe recruitment, training and a code of conduct; checks are only accurate to the date processed, so they are never the only safeguard; consider barred list referral after dismissal for harm

title: Time Well Spent 2023: at a glance
supports: Opened with WebFetch (report published 27 June 2023). 92% of recent formal volunteers satisfied (96% in 2019); 77% likely to continue (80% in 2019); 25% of dissatisfied vs 76% of satisfied likely to continue; 37% of those unlikely to continue cite less time; 19% to 26% feel it is too much like paid work; 34% of non-volunteers avoid ongoing commitment; worry about cost rose from 5% to 14%; 31% volunteer online or by phone; 55% say expenses would be repaid. Sample details are in an appendix not read

title: Community Life Survey 2024/25: Volunteering and charitable giving
publisher: Department for Culture, Media and Sport (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 10 December 2025, updated 31 July 2026). England, adults 16+, fieldwork October 2024 to March 2025: formal volunteering 17% monthly and 28.4% yearly; informal 24% monthly and 44% yearly; formal yearly volunteering was 45% in 2013/14

title: Value of volunteer time
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Released 21 April 2026 with the Do Good Institute: US estimated value of a volunteer hour $36.14 for 2025 (preliminary), up 3.9% on 2024, based on BLS average hourly earnings of production and non-supervisory workers plus fringe benefits

title: Fact Sheet #14A: Non-profit organizations and the Fair Labor Standards Act
publisher: US Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch (fact sheet dated August 2015). Volunteers for charitable nonprofits serve without expecting pay; they generally cannot volunteer in commercial activities such as a gift shop, should not displace paid workers, and paid staff cannot volunteer to do the same work they are paid for

title: DBS checks: guidance for applicants
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). The four check levels (basic, standard, enhanced, enhanced with barred lists) and what each shows; voluntary organisations can request checks; a check has no official expiry date; employers can check an Update Service subscriber's certificate online

title: DBS checks: guidance for employers, voluntary organisations and third parties
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 27 March 2013, updated 5 October 2026 for the October 2026 fee change). Fees: basic and standard GBP 20, enhanced and enhanced with barred lists GBP 41; asking for a higher check than the law allows is unlawful; volunteer definition from the 2002 regulations; standard and enhanced checks free for volunteers who meet the conditions; Update Service for standard and enhanced only, joining within 30 days of issue; minimum age to apply 16

title: DBS check: application process for volunteers
supports: Opened with WebFetch (first published 6 July 2015, updated 5 October 2026). Basic checks cost GBP 20 even for a volunteer role; the Update Service was referenced for volunteers on 1 July 2026

title: Handling of DBS certificate information
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 4 July 2018). Store securely with controlled access; share only with those entitled; use only for the purpose requested; keep no longer than necessary after the decision; destroy securely; keep no photocopy or image; you may record date of issue, name, check type, position, reference number and the decision

title: Safeguarding and protecting people for charities and trustees
publisher: Charity Commission for England and Wales (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 6 December 2017, updated 8 October 2026). Policies reviewed at least yearly and after serious incidents and made public; code of conduct for staff and volunteers; risk assess each role for DBS eligibility and level; report concerns to police, local authority or LADO and serious incidents to the Commission; from 1 September 2026 the supervision exemption for regulated work with children no longer applies

title: Protecting Vulnerable Groups (PVG) scheme
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). In Scotland, joining the PVG scheme run by Disclosure Scotland is a legal requirement for regulated roles with children or protected adults; membership lasts five years; organisations must report harmful behaviour to Disclosure Scotland

title: Find out which DBS check is right for your employee
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). The eligibility tool is for organisations in England and Wales; Scotland and Northern Ireland have separate processes

title: Charities and meetings (CC48)
publisher: Charity Commission for England and Wales (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 1 March 2012, updated 19 July 2024). Follow the governing document exactly; notice by post, email only if the document allows and members agreed; clear days; at least 3 weeks if no period is set; companies at least 14 days for general meetings; quorum rules; virtual or hybrid only if permitted; simple majority if silent; proxy and postal votes only if permitted; what minutes record; minute retention of 6 or 10 years by structure

title: Data (Use and Access) Act factsheet: Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations
publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (published 27 June 2025). Section 114 lets charities send marketing emails and texts to people who showed interest in their work, with a chance to opt out when details are collected and at any time after

title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025: plans for commencement
publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (GOV.UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 12 October 2026). The majority of Part 5 data protection and privacy provisions came into force on 5 February 2026 (Commencement No. 6 Regulations 2026); the page does not list the charity soft opt-in by name

title: Marketing and advertising: the law, direct marketing
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). Marketing emails to individuals need their permission; each message identifies the sender and offers an easy unsubscribe; check the Telephone Preference Service before calls; keep proof of what people agreed to

title: Data protection and online privacy
supports: Opened with WebFetch (last checked by the EU on 5 August 2026). Consent needs a clear opt-in action and information first; marketing emails need prior consent except similar products to existing customers; people can object to direct marketing and withdraw consent at any time

title: WildApricot pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. No free plan; a 60-day free trial with no card, after which an account not upgraded is deleted; plans tiered by contacts from 100 to 50,000, all with the same features; monthly or yearly billing

title: Membership management software
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated feature page). Members renew online; Direct Debit, card and wallet options on sign-up; a Gift Aid donation can be added to a membership; automatic welcome emails or letters; Mailchimp connection

title: Volunteer management
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated feature page). Branded application forms, records of availability, references and emergency contacts, a field to store a copy of the latest DBS certificate, hours logged by volunteers through a portal, automatic thanks on application; no rota feature described

title: Handle failed payments
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated help doc). After a failed renewal Memberful emails the member, retries up to four times 12 hours apart, and deactivates the subscription if payment is not collected 48 hours after the failure; it warns members when a card will expire before renewal

title: Membership options
publisher: Buddle (the new home of Sport England's Club Matters)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated). Fees should cover costs but stay affordable; subsidised, monthly, pay-as-you-go, family and volunteer discounts; confidential bursaries; a checklist before changing subs; collecting subs firmly but kindly; Direct Debit set-up needs a sponsoring bank or an outside service

title: Your stories: Bexley RFC
supports: Opened with WebFetch (undated case study). Bexley RFC, short of playing numbers and volunteer skills, asked its local Volunteer Centre for help and recruited four new volunteers: two made recruitment posters, handouts and a video, and two trained as first aiders
